description_en: The site is located in the village of Kimugāũ, east of the Dailekh distrcit headquarter of Narayana. The temples are found in a corn field near the motorable road linking Dailekh-Narayana to the Lohore Khola.The site of the Kimugāũ temples is constituted of sevenśikharatemples, organised in three groups of two anf three monuments. It is likely that some monuments are missing, or that the architectural program could not be completed. This is indicated by the northern group of temples (temples 001, 002 and 003), where the monuments are organised around a central temple (001, oriented to the south) and subsidiary temples (002 and 003) built around, facing the central temple. This plan suggests that two otherśikharaswere built to the east and south of temple 001, thus creating apañcadevalaplan. This setting reflects thesmārtaworship of Hindu gods. Temples 004 and 007 may have also been part of apañcadevalaplan.In West Nepalśikharatemples are known asdevala. Thepañcadevalaplan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which corresponds to the area controlled by the Rāskoṭi kings. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century (Andolfatto 2019, 79-90). In the absence of epigraphic records it is possible to date the Kimugāũ Pañcadevala between the 13th and the 15th century.The sanctums are all empty but a picture of temple 003 taken by Marc Gaborieau in 1968 shows that it contained a stoneśivaliṅga.The temples are mentioned inSharma 1972, 22, 24 andSharma 2012, 128-129.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
